What Prep are you most proud of?

I live someplace where hoarding items doesn't make a lot of sense because there is a real danger of a natural disaster wiping the land ( has happened before).

However, I'm really proud of the skills I have acquired. I learned to process coconuts for oil, meat, water and flour this year. I also learned to identify local medicinal plants. I've also starting to learn to sprout different types of tree seeds. I know how to make fiber and tools out of bamboo. Adding this to my knowledge of fishing and farming I already have, I'm not gonna die if the worst happens.

Probably my bugout bag. I've put a LOT of work into it and have tried it out many times. I'm quite comfortable with it and its contents. Its a bit on the heavy side, but I have it ready for extended use, which makes it heavy.

I have a handful of really awesome bug out locations.

When I was a kid, I would have about 5 different "Forts" in the forest in about a Kilometer radius from my house, where my friends and I could play "Cowboys and Indians". I never outgrew that, so I'm still doing it.

Now, my Forts are more like hunting / camping designations. My favorite is one that is waaay the fuck out in the desert in a canyon. I've spoken about briefly in /v/preppers when I was talking about my water catchment system (I don't remember why it was brought up specifically).

Anyway, it's like, Imagine the "Swiss Family Robenson" if they lived in a canyon full of giant boulders instead of a tree house. I took some time to delibrately plant native edible plants here and there. I've got my water catchment system. I have drilled some climbing anchors into the boulders to hang a hammock and a tarp for shelter. Buried some supplies and tools. etc.

The best part is, once everything is taken down, if someone wandered by, they wouldn't even know this is a bug out location. It's just rocks and native plants and a hidden water catchment system.

All I need now is some Pirates to fight against and I'll be good.

I'll refrain from boasting about any offensive/defensive capabilities I may/may not have. I will say I am proud of the fact that I've gotten my household plant/vegetable waste composting routine down solid. It typically takes me about 6 to 8 months to build up 5 or more pounds of the stuff when dried out. I've got about three gallons of water storage capacity I will eventually expand on, but lack space to accommodate doing so at present. Now I'm focusing on household paper, plastics, and metals waste recovery, in that very order.
